_sources.schd_carryover_long: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet, long-term section: L9 = Schedule D line 15 loss as positive = $4,000; L10 = gain from Schedule D line 7 = $0 (it is a loss); L11 = L4 - L5 = 3000 - 6000, zero or less so $0; L12 = 0 + 0 = $0; L13 = 4000 - 0 = $4,000 long-term carryover (untouched, because the allowance was fully absorbed by the short-term loss)
_sources.schd_carryover_short: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet (Instructions for Schedule D), figured line by line: L1 = Form 1040 line 15 = $41,250; L2 = Schedule D line 21 loss as positive = $3,000; L3 = 41250 + 3000 = $44,250; L4 = smaller of L2/L3 = $3,000 (the allowance actually absorbed); L5 = Schedule D line 7 loss as positive = $6,000; L6 = gain from Schedule D line 15 = $0 (it is a loss); L7 = 3000 + 0 = $3,000; L8 = 6000 - 3000 = $3,000 short-term carryover. The $3,000 allowance is consumed against the short-term loss first.
_sources.schd_net_capital_gain: QDCG Worksheet line 3 requires Schedule D lines 15 and 16 to be gains; line 15 is a loss, so $0 — Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet (Instructions for Form 1040, line 16)

description: Single filer; one W-2 ($60,000 wages, $6,000 withheld); one 1099-B with a short-term loss (proceeds $4,000 / basis $10,000) and a long-term loss (proceeds $6,000 / basis $10,000). Exercises the Schedule D combination, the IRC 1211(b) capital-loss limit, and the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet. Money values below are integer cents.
